gaps.construct: atomic.Bool field and Mutex field inside Once
gaps.description: The doc rules out shared mutable values between tasks and so has no atomic or lock types; `Atomic Bool` and `Mutex` are invented.

gaps.construct: one *Once used by many goroutines at once
gaps.description: `editable` implies exclusive access and `together` rejects two tasks changing one value; there is no way to declare a value intended for concurrent mutation, so `shared` is invented.
No memory-ordering or atomic-operation vocabulary; `atomically load done of o` is invented.
No type for an operation value; `an operation` is invented, and calling f inside do_slow needs an invented call form too.

gaps.construct: Do has whatever effects f has
gaps.description: `uses` must name capabilities; there is no way to say the effects come from a parameter, so `uses f` is invented.

gaps.construct: documented guarantee: f runs at most once, and every Do returns only after f has finished
gaps.description: This is a property across concurrent calls; `ensure` and `at entry` describe one call, so the core contract of sync.Once cannot be written.

gaps.construct: defer o.done.Store(true) and defer o.m.Unlock() in doSlow
gaps.description: `hold` covers releasing a resource on every exit but there is no general deferred statement, so the store-after-f ordering cannot be expressed.
No methods; the receiver becomes a labelled parameter, which changes call sites from o.Do(f) to `do f with o`.
No inlining control, so the reason for the split disappears; it is kept only to mirror the original.

doc_rules_contradicted: Because values are never shared mutably between tasks, there is nothing for a lock to protect, and no way to forget one.
With no `uses` line the operation is pure (Do's effects depend on f and cannot be named)
notes: sync.Once is not expressible in the doc's model at all: the model forbids the shared mutable state that is the whole point of the type. Scribe needs either a library-level trusted primitive (a `once` or lazy-initialisation construct with a stated contract) or an explicit shared-state type with a concurrency contract language. Note that the bug the Go comment warns about (the CAS-only version) is exactly the kind of cross-call guarantee Scribe's single-call ensure lines cannot express or check.
